convoLines.text: «Halo! Kamu... siapa namamu?»
«Benar.» They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«Kamu orang baik.» (you catch 'baik' — good) They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«Kebaikan ini takkan kulupakan.» (you catch 'Kebaikan' — kindness, 'kulupakan' — forget) You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «Di sini tidur di mana? Aman?» (you catch 'Aman' — safe)
Yosina laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Itu benar. Benar sekali." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Hei... unasema Kiswahili? Hapana? ...lahaula.» "Hello?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Ndiyo, ndiyo, hasa.» They nod back, slowly.
«Wewe ni mtu mwema.» (you catch 'mwema' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Asante kwa kuwa hapa.» (you catch 'Asante' — thank you) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «Wewe ndiye... kiongozi hapa?» (you catch 'kiongozi' — leader)
Wanjiru laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Ndiyo, uko sahihi." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
«Hei... bisa bahasa Indonesia? Tidak? ...sialan.» (you catch 'Tidak' — no)
«Ya, saya merasakan hal yang sama.» (Yes, I feel the same way. — you're fairly sure) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«Terima kasih sudah di sini.» (Thank you for being here. — you're fairly sure) A smile, tired but real. "Please?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Semuanya akan baik-baik saja.» (Everything will be just fine. — you're fairly sure) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Kamu... pemimpin di sini?» (Are you... the leader here? — you're fairly sure)
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
«Habari! Wewe... jina lako nani?» (you catch 'Habari' — hello)
«Ndiyo, uko sahihi.» (Yes, you're correct. — you're fairly sure) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«Sitaisahau wema huu.» (I will not forget this kindness. — you're fairly sure) A smile, tired but real.
«Kila kitu kitakuwa sawa.» (Everything will be okay. — you're fairly sure) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «Una chakula? Chochote?» (Do you have food? Anything? — you're fairly sure)
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you — sorry. I keep thinking about them."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Hazel. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
Hazel looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"Moshe owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I oil boots on rest days. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Hazel grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Hazel is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"We both stood at the treeline. Moshe held it. I keep replaying my part, looking for the step I missed."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sleep's gone strange. I clean up other people's messes quietly at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Hazel nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Can I be honest? Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Between us — Forget it — go on, I'm listening."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Moshe killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid. You know?"
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now."
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I dreamed Moshe was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Moshe said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"Still on what's been happening. You doing okay?"
"Yeah. Me too, if I'm honest." A small, real smile.

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Mateo Hughes is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Mateo is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Mateo Hughes is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Mateo kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Mateo's gone." Yosina looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Mateo." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Moshe blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Boiling Water (Level 1). Rolling boil for 1 minute kills most pathogens. The simplest safe water.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Mateo Hughes, 41 days. The mantle passes to Moshe Singh.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Moshe Singh, 56 — a line cook. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Bird Whisperer, Green Whisper, Echo Location.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Mateo — and Mateo is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Hazel, Yosina, Ursula and 2 more speak for Moshe — "Mateo trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Moshe before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
